# Introduction

In order to analyze BCR and TCR clones in a ccRCC tumors samples at a scale closer to single cell, we used the [SpatialVDJ](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adf8486?url_ver=Z39.88-2003&rfr_id=ori:rid:crossref.org&rfr_dat=cr_pub%20%200pubmed) method developped by Engblom et al. It is an adaptation of Visium (10X Genomics) on Fresh Frozen slices with a capture of BCR and TCR full length cDNA, before fragmentation, and long read sequencing using PacBio sequencing platform. On an other part, spatial gene expression is also performed.

For a first analysis we choose 4 tumor samples from BioniKK cohort from 3 patients (2 samples are 2 blocks coming from the same tumor : SP_LHD6US & SP_0V2O6G). Spatial gene expression (**SpatialGEX** = Visium spatial transcriptomics short reads sequencing) sample position on slide :   

- A1 : SP_LHD6US  
- B1 : SP_0V2O6G  
- C1 : SP_0O0B5S  
- D1 : SP_R9MS02  

The goal is to analyze BCR and TCR relationships regarding to TLS : clonal evolution (expansion, SHM, CSR) vs TLS at spatial resolution.

For Long Read - the sequencing depth of the first run was low for 3 samples and thus a second sequencing run was performed on the same library (only for the 3 samples with low depth) and the result was quite the same ... We then choose to perform another experiment of **SpatialVDJ** on the same Visium cDNA, ie : pre-amplification PCR, xGen IDT SpatialVDJ capture, SMRTbell library preparation (with some adaptation here) and finaly PacBio Sequell sequencing. Apparently this 3rd run was much better (the SMRTbell were also better in the QC) and a much higher depth was obtain for all samples (data deposited and analyzed).


Sections :

- **Preprocess** :  
1/ All pre-process step of **SpatialGEX** data (Seurat spot QC, BayesSpace spatial clustering, Starfysh cell type deconvolution, SpaTopic CellTopic and Meta Topic generation). Some plot were also generated along these steps : **2B, 2C, S7A,S7B,S7C,S7D, S7E, S7F**  
2/ All pre-process step of **SpatialVDJ** data (Long read preparation, IgBlast alignment, post-alignment QC, IGH form identification, collapse duplicates in clonotypes).  
3/ Generate a merged Seurat object with anonymized id, all spot from all patients, and all metadata generated from SpatialGEX and SpatialVDJ pre-processing, and necessary to reproduce main plot : BayesSpace cluster, Starfysh deconvolution values, TLS signature scores, CellTopic and MetaTopic (meta cluster) from SpaTopic, number of clonotype for each chain, each isotype and each form (when identified unambiguously as BCR or antibody) in each spots. This file is shared as **20260721_Seurat_merged_SpatialGEX_annotated_metadata.rds**.   
4/ Generate a clonotypes table for SpatialVDJ clonotypes, processed with Immcantation pipeline, and matching the SpatialGEX Seurat object. This file is shared as **20260721_airr_igblast-db_full_database.tsv**. 
5/ Generate a clonotypes table for MiXCR reconstructed clonotypes from 12 ccRCC Visium V1 from Meylan et al, 2022, Immunity. This file is shared as **20260722_clonotype_spatial_mut_Immunity12ccRCC_anonymized.rds**.  

- **Reload merged dataset** :  
Reload data to generate plots.

- **Figures** : 
Script to reproduce Figure 2 and S6 as well as some panels of S7 (many panel of S7 are included in pre-process files if one want to reproduce these plots also).

```{r,eval=T}
# from Maxime Meylan
plot_contingency <- function(data,
           variables = c("TLS_pos", "HBV"),
           hide_legend = F,
           text_size=6,
           create_labels = T,
           inverse_factor2=F,
           order_factor=NULL,
           palette = NA,
           test_name = c("chisq.test", "fisher.test")[1],
           labs = c(xlab = "",
                    ylab = "",
                    legend_title = ""),
           hide_test = F,
           title = ""){
    if(inverse_factor2){
      data[,variables[2]] <- factor(data[,variables[2]],levels=rev(levels(data[,variables[2]])))
    }
    cont_table <- table(data[,variables[1]],data[,variables[2]])
    #clean data table to avoid empty rows
    non_empty_rows <- rowSums(cont_table)!=0
    cont_table <- cont_table[non_empty_rows,]

    if(create_labels){
      #sapply(levels(factor(data[,variables[2]])), function(x) paste(variables[2],x,sep="_"))
      colnames(cont_table) <- sapply(levels(factor(data[,variables[2]])), function(x) paste(variables[2],x,sep="_"))
      rownames(cont_table) <- sapply(levels(factor(data[,variables[1]])), function(x) paste(variables[1],x,sep="_"))
    }
  if(test_name != "fisher.test" & test_name != "chisq.test"){
    stop("incorrect test, valid options are fisher.test or chisq.test")
  }
  if(test_name == "fisher.test"){
    error_test <-  if(class(try(fisher.test(cont_table),silent=T)) == "try-error"){
      test_res <- fisher.test(cont_table,simulate.p.value = T)
    }else{
      test_res <- fisher.test(cont_table)
    }
  }
  if(test_name == "chisq.test"){
    test_res <- chisq.test(cont_table)
  }
  #make sure there is a matrix (enough values in both sides)
  if(!is.null(dim(cont_table))){
    cont_table_perc <-apply(cont_table,1,function(x) {
      res <- x / sum(x) *100
    })
    cont_table_m <- melt(cont_table_perc)
    cont_table_m$Var1 <- factor(cont_table_m$Var1)
    p <- ggplot(data=cont_table_m, aes(x=Var2,y=value,fill=Var1,label=value))
    p <- p + geom_bar(stat="identity",width=0.95)
    #to reverse order of bars
    #p <- p + geom_bar(stat="identity",width=0.95,position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE))
    p <- p + geom_text(label = paste0(as.vector(t(cont_table)),"\n(",format(cont_table_m$value,digits = 1),"%)"),
                       position = position_stack(vjust = .5),size=text_size)
    p <- p + theme_minimal()

    if(any(!is.na(palette))){
      p <- p + scale_fill_manual(values = palette)
    }
    #p <- p + theme(legend.title = element_blank())#,axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
    p <- p + guides(fill=guide_legend(title=labs[3]))
    if(hide_test){
      p <- p + labs(subtitle=paste("p = ",format(test_res$p.value,digits=3),sep=" "),title=title,x=labs[1],y=labs[2])
      if(test_res$p.value < 0.05 ) p <- p + theme(plot.subtitle=element_text(face="bold"))
    }else{
      p <- p + labs(subtitle=paste(test_name, " p = ",format(test_res$p.value,digits=3),sep=" "),title=title,x=labs[1],y=labs[2])
      if(test_res$p.value < 0.05 ) p <- p + theme(plot.subtitle=element_text(face="bold"))
    }

    if(hide_legend){
      p <- p + guides(fill=FALSE)
    }
  }else{
    p <- ggplot()
    test_res <-1
  }
  return(list(p,test_res,cont_table))

}
```

# Preprocess - Not rendered

All script bellow are run only one time - not re run for plot/render markdown.

## SpatialGEX 

### Quality filter and BayesSpace clustering - Contains plot for Supplementary S7A

Visium Spatial gene expression (SpatialGEX) quality filter is adapted from a script from [Meylan et al 2022](https://github.com/maximemeylan/Meylan_et_al_2022/blob/main/00_visium_preprocessing.R)

- Calculate the percentage of reads that map to the mitochondrial genome (Low-quality / dying cells often exhibit extensive mitochondrial contamination).  
- Filter out genes that are counted less that 5 times within the sum of all cells.  
- Filter out Spatial spots featuring more than 30% of mitochondrial genes.  
- Filter out Spatial spots having less than 300 expressed genes.  
- Remove genes coded on the mitochondrial genome. 

Spot clustering was perfomred with the BayesSpace method (spatial clustering) by : 
Reproduce [Preprocess](https://github.com/CIG-spatialLandscape/spatialHallmarks_paper/blob/main/Preprocess.R#L74) script, [EnhanceST.R](https://github.com/CIG-spatialLandscape/spatialHallmarks_paper/blob/main/EnhanceST.R) script and [GeneImputation.R](https://github.com/CIG-spatialLandscape/spatialHallmarks_paper/blob/main/GeneImputation.R) script from Sibai and Cervilla (Unraveling the spatial architecture of Cancer Hallmarks) which has used the package [BayesSpace](http://www.ezstatconsulting.com/BayesSpace/articles/ji_SCC.html) from Zhao et al (2021 - Nature Biotechnology - Spatial transcriptomics at subspot resolution with BayesSpace).
NB : The enhance resolution from BayesSpace was only used for visualization of some genes (not included in the final article) and not for any analysis.

 The following script with qPlot function was used to plot the q plot presented in Figure Supplmentary **S7A** (bottom : for slide SP_LHD6US)

```{r,eval=FALSE}
#@ Note : all the QC plot here can be reproduced but are not included in the file shared // the path corresponds to the original location were plot were saved. Need to be adapted if one reproduce the following script

### code for systematic analysis 
slide_list <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id

# Preprocess samples, transform to SingleCellExperiment object and run clustering
# Adapt from : Author: Sergi Cervilla* & Mustafa Sibai*

# create directory to store BayesSpace results
if(!file.exists(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/"))) dir.create(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/")) 

for(slide in slide_list){
  
  #create directyry to store results per slide
  if(!file.exists(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide))) dir.create(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide)) 
  
  #create directory to store figures
  if(!file.exists(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures"))) dir.create(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures")) 
  
  #create directory to store RDS files
  if(!file.exists(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS"))) dir.create(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS")) 

  
    raw_data_directory <- paste0("PATH/",slide,"/outs/")
  STobject <- Seurat::Load10X_Spatial(raw_data_directory)
  
  TissuePosition <- read.csv(paste0(raw_data_directory,"spatial/tissue_positions.csv"),header = TRUE)
  rownames(TissuePosition) <- TissuePosition$barcode
  STobject <- AddMetaData(object= STobject,metadata = TissuePosition[rownames(STobject@meta.data),c("in_tissue")],col.name ="in_tissue" )
  
  p<-(SpatialDimPlot(STobject,group.by = c("in_tissue"),alpha=0)+theme(legend.position = "none"))
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/Slide_without_spot.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")
  
  p<-(SpatialDimPlot(STobject,group.by = c("in_tissue")))
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/SpotSelected_prefiltering.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")
  
   #Spot with less than 300 features
  STobject$num.features.filtered <- ifelse(STobject$nFeature_Spatial > 300,yes = "> 300","<= 300")
  
  p<-((SpatialFeaturePlot(STobject, features = c("nCount_Spatial")) + theme(legend.position = "right")) / (SpatialFeaturePlot(STobject, features = c("nFeature_Spatial")) + theme(legend.position = "right")) / (SpatialDimPlot(STobject,group.by = "num.features.filtered",facet.highlight = F) + theme(legend.position = "right")))
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/FeatureFilter_prefiltering.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")
  
  # Collect all genes coded on the mitochondrial genome
  mt.genes <- grep(pattern = "^MT-", x = rownames(STobject), value = TRUE)
  STobject$percent.mito <- (Matrix::colSums(STobject@assays$Spatial$counts[mt.genes, ])/Matrix::colSums(STobject@assays$Spatial$counts))*100
  STobject$percent.mito.filtered <- factor(ifelse(STobject$percent.mito< 30,yes = "< 30%",">= 30%"),levels = c(">= 30%", "< 30%"))

  p<-((SpatialFeaturePlot(STobject, features = c("percent.mito")) + theme(legend.position = "right")) / (SpatialDimPlot(STobject,group.by = "percent.mito.filtered",facet.highlight = F) + theme(legend.position = "right")))
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/PercentMito_prefiltering.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")

  
  
  # remove mitochondrial, ribosomal and gene counted less than 5 time in sum all spot
  # Eventually remove non-coding genes 

  selected_genes <- names(which(Matrix::rowSums(STobject@assays$Spatial$counts )>5))
  #keep protein coding genes
  # selected_genes <- protein_genes[protein_genes %in% selected_genes]
  #remove ribosomal genes
  selected_genes <- selected_genes[!grepl("^RP[SL][[:digit:]]|^RPLP[[:digit:]]|^RPSA", selected_genes)]
  #remove mitochondrial genes
  selected_genes <- selected_genes[!grepl("^MT-", selected_genes)]
  
  
  STobject <- suppressWarnings(subset(STobject,features =selected_genes, subset = nFeature_Spatial > 300 & percent.mito < 30))
  
  p<- VlnPlot(STobject, features = c("nFeature_Spatial", "nCount_Spatial"),layer = "counts")
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/VlnPlot_nCount_nFeature_postfiltering.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")
  
  p<-((SpatialFeaturePlot(STobject, features = c("nCount_Spatial")) + theme(legend.position = "right")) / (SpatialFeaturePlot(STobject, features = c("nFeature_Spatial")) + theme(legend.position = "right")))
  ggsave(plot = p,filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/SpatialPlot_nCount_nFeature_postfiltering.pdf"),width = 4.92,height = 4.17,units = "in")
  
  #Normalization of the data returning all genes (SCT)
  STobject <- SCTransform(STobject,return.only.var.genes = FALSE, variable.features.n = NULL, variable.features.rv.th = 1.1, assay = "Spatial")

  saveRDS(STobject, paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_seurat_postfilter_sct.rds"))
  
  
  ########## Create SingleCellExperiment object with SCT normalization ###########
  
  #Create SCE object by transfering SCT assay and metadata (Spatial coordinates)
  ST_sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(x = STobject,assay = "SCT")
  
  ## Make the assay name as SCT (logcount)
  ST_sce@assays@data@listData[["SCT"]] <- ST_sce@assays@data@listData[["logcounts"]] 
  
  ## Add colData to the SingleCellExperiment object
  colData <- TissuePosition[TissuePosition$in_tissue > 0, ]
  colData <- colData[rownames(ST_sce@colData),] #order the same way and keep only filtered spots
  colnames(colData) <- c("spot", "in_tissue", "row","col",
                        "imagerow","imagecol") 
  
  identical(rownames(colData(ST_sce)),rownames(colData)) # should be T
  colData(ST_sce) <- cbind(colData(ST_sce),colData)
  
  metadata(ST_sce)$BayesSpace.data <- list()
  metadata(ST_sce)$BayesSpace.data$platform <- "Visium"
  metadata(ST_sce)$BayesSpace.data$is.enhanced <- FALSE
  
  
  # Cluster with BayesSpace
  set.seed(100)
  # Compute top 2000 HVGs and 15 PCA using the SCT data
  ST_sce <- spatialPreprocess(ST_sce, platform = "Visium", n.PCs = 15,
                              n.HVGs = 2000, log.normalize = F, assay.type = "SCT")
  
  # Find q for clusters
  ST_sce <- qTune(ST_sce, qs = seq(2, 20), platform = "Visium",d =15)
  
    # The following script with qPlot function was used to plot the q plot presented in Figure Supplmentary S7A (bottom : for slide SP_LHD6US)
  p <- qPlot(ST_sce)
  
  pdf(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/BayesQplot.pdf"), width = 8, height = 7)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  saveRDS(ST_sce, paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_beforeClustering.rds"))
  
  
  #keep some memory
  ## remove all object but c("FileID","ImmcantationFolder","RawReadFolder")
  rm(list=setdiff(ls(),c("res_folder","slide_list")))
  gc()
  
}
  

```

The following script with clusterPlot function was used to plot the spatial plot presented in Figure Supplmentary **S7A** (top : for slide SP_LHD6US)

```{r,eval=FALSE}
### code for systematic analysis 
slide_list <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id


## Define q base on qPlot
slide_list_q <- c(12,10,11,12) ##should be adapted according to plot p (NB : initally q was set to 6 for SP_R9MS02 but we observed that it generated consistent cluster with histology by increasing to a number of cluster similar to other slides, ie 12)
names(slide_list_q) <- slide_list


for(slide in slide_list){
  
  #number of clusters
  q = slide_list_q[[slide]] 
  #number of PCA
  d = 15
  
  #Reload rds
  ST_sce <- readRDS(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_beforeClustering.rds"))
  
  # Run the clustering 
  ST_sce <- spatialCluster(ST_sce, q=q, d=d, init.method = "kmeans", platform = "Visium", nrep = 50000, gamma = 3)
  ST_sce$spatial.cluster <- as.factor(ST_sce$spatial.cluster)
  
  # Plot Spatial Cluster at spot resolution
  
  ###### The following script with clusterPlot function was used to plot the spatial plot presented in Figure Supplmentary S7A (top : for slide SP_LHD6US)
  
  palette <- RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(q, name = "Paired")
  p <- clusterPlot(ST_sce, palette = palette, size=0.05) + labs(title = "Spot-level clustering") + coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse() # + coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse() to rotate in the same order as the HE/Seurat object
  pdf(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/Spot_level_clustering.pdf"), width = 8, height = 7)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  saveRDS(ST_sce, paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_afterClustering.rds"))

  
  # Use BayesSpace enhancing algorithm in Visium Spatial transcriptomics data
  ## Adapted from Author: Sergi Cervilla* & Mustafa Sibai*
  #signle cell experiment object at spot level
  #check image orientation - swap imagerow and imagecol
  if (cor(ST_sce$imagecol, ST_sce$col) < 0.9) {
    tmp <- ST_sce$imagecol
    ST_sce$imagecol <- ST_sce$imagerow
    ST_sce$imagerow <- tmp
  }
  #enhance single cell experiment object
  ST_sce.enhanced <- spatialEnhance(ST_sce, q=length(unique(ST_sce$spatial.cluster)), d=15, platform="Visium", init=ST_sce$spatial.cluster, 
                                    nrep=200000, gamma=3, verbose = TRUE,  jitter_prior=0.3, save.chain=TRUE)
  #save enhanced object (without gene imputation)
  saveRDS(ST_sce.enhanced, paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_enhanced.rds"))
  
  
  
  # Impute genes at sub-spot resolution
  ## Adapted from Author: Sergi Cervilla* & Mustafa Sibai*
  #load single cell experiment object at spot level (with gene expression)
  # ST_sce <- readRDS(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce.rds"))
  # #load single cell experiment object at sub-spot level (without gene expression)
  # ST_sce.enhanced <- readRDS(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_enhanced.rds"))
  # 
  #Impute genes at sub-spot resolution
  ST_sce.enhanced <- enhanceFeatures(ST_sce.enhanced, ST_sce,
                                  model="xgboost",
                                  nrounds=100,
                                  assay.type = "SCT")
  #save file
  saveRDS(ST_sce.enhanced, paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/RDS/",slide,"_sce_enhanced_geneImputed.rds"))
  
  # Plot it in render ...
  p <- clusterPlot(ST_sce.enhanced, palette = palette, size=0.05) + labs(title = "Subspot-level clustering") + coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse() # + coord_flip() + scale_y_reverse() to rotate in the same order as the HE/Seurat object
  pdf(paste0(res_folder,"02_BayesSpace/",slide,"/figures/Subspot_level_clustering.pdf"), width = 8, height = 7)
  print(p)
  dev.off()
  
  
  #keep some memory
  ## remove all object but c("FileID","ImmcantationFolder","RawReadFolder")
  rm(list=setdiff(ls(),c("res_folder","slide_list")))
  gc()
}
```

### Spot deconvolution using starfysh

Spot single cell deconvolution was performed with Starfysh according to a [script adapted by Isaias Hernandez](https://github.com/iS4i4S/GABA-TLS/blob/main/Figures/Starfysh_deconvolution.html) for the article: Hernandez-Verdin, Calvez, Sun, et al, 2026 (see main paper bibliography)

The exact same script was applied, with same cell type signatures. The only modification was the identifier and path. The adjusted script (provided as a not rendered script to hide patient original unanonymized id) where some can be found in the repository under the name **ccRCC_starfysh_deconvolution.ipynb**.

### Merge BayesSpace clustering with starfysh deconvolution value and hubs

create a seurat object where BayesSpace clusters (derived from single cell experiment object) and starfysh deconvolution values are annotated. ie a Seurat object with filtered spots, SCT normalized gene expression value, BayesSpace cluster tag, Starfysh deconvolution value and Starfysh Hub tag.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
# NB : again this script is provided for consistency in all chunk, but only the final annotated seurat is provided, with anonymized id. 

SampleId <- Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id

IDmatch <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id
names(IDmatch) <- SampleId

TLSsign <- readRDS("PATH/TLS_signatures.rds")


# Load starfysh result and concatenate them: see corresponding python script
Starfysh <- read.csv("PATH/Starfysh_integrated_proportions.csv",row.names = 1) 

CellTypes <- colnames(Starfysh)

StarfyshHub <- read.csv("PATH/Starfysh_integrated_hubs.csv",row.names = 1) 

if(!identical(rownames(Starfysh),rownames(StarfyshHub))){
  stop("olala")
}

Starfysh <- cbind(Starfysh,StarfyshHub)


#Split starfysh results by sample
Starfysh <- split(Starfysh,substr(rownames(Starfysh),20,nchar(rownames(Starfysh))))

# Remove Id from rownames to retrieve only the spatial barcode as it is in Seurat
Starfysh <- lapply(Starfysh,function(df){
  rownames(df)<- substr(rownames(df),start = 1,stop = 18)
  df
})


#iterate per sample
for(file in FileID){
  #Load final Seurat object
  SeuratSCT <- readRDS(paste0("PATH/",IDmatch[[file]],"/RDS/",IDmatch[[file]],"_seurat_postfilter_sct.rds")) # load seurat preprocessed

  
  #First Add the classical seurat_clusters : optional / not used then
  SeuratSCT <- RunPCA(SeuratSCT, assay = "SCT", verbose = FALSE)
  SeuratSCT <- FindNeighbors(SeuratSCT, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30)
  SeuratSCT <- FindClusters(SeuratSCT, resolution = 1.5)
  SeuratSCT <- RunUMAP(SeuratSCT, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30)
  
  # Get the correct starfysh result
  StarfyshPatient <- Starfysh[[IDmatch[[file]]]]
  StarfyshPatient <- StarfyshPatient[colnames(SeuratSCT),] # Keep only spots present in Seurat processed
  StarfyshPatient$hub <- factor(StarfyshPatient$hub,levels = sort(unique(StarfyshPatient$hub)))
  colnames(StarfyshPatient) <-paste0("Starfysh_",colnames(StarfyshPatient))
  
  # Add metadata
  SeuratSCT <- AddMetaData(SeuratSCT,StarfyshPatient)
  
  ## Same for BayesSpace cluster and save them ...
  #Load sce object from BayesSpace with spatial cluster at spot level
  sce <- readRDS(paste0("PATH/","02_BayesSpace/",IDmatch[[file]],"/RDS/",IDmatch[[file]],"_sce_afterClustering.rds"))
  if(!identical(rownames(sce@colData),colnames(SeuratSCT)))stop(paste(file,"olalalalala"))
  Cluster <- data.frame(BayesSpace_cluster=sce@colData$spatial.cluster)
  rownames(Cluster) <- rownames(sce@colData)
  
  # Add BayesSpace cluster to Seurat metadata
  SeuratSCT <- AddMetaData(object= SeuratSCT,
                        metadata = Cluster)
  
  # Compute TLS signatures scores as mean or sum of the gene of the signatures included in the noramlized spots
  IdSign<-names(TLSsign)
  names(IdSign)<-IdSign
  TLSplot<-list()
  TLSplot[["HE"]]<-SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features ="nCount_Spatial",pt.size.factor = 0)+theme(legend.position = "none" )+labs(title = "H&E") 
  ggsave(plot = TLSplot$HE,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/",file,"_HEonly.pdf"),
         width = 3,height = 4)
  
  
  for(idsign in IdSign){
    sign<-TLSsign[[idsign]]
    intersect_tls_sign <- intersect(sign,rownames(SeuratSCT)) 
    # and add to metadata scaled mean or sum of gene expression
    if(length(intersect_tls_sign)==1){
      SeuratSCT <- AddMetaData(SeuratSCT,SeuratSCT[["SCT"]]@scale.data[intersect_tls_sign,],col.name = paste(idsign,"only",sep = "_")) 
      TLSplot[[idsign]] <- ((SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features =paste(idsign,"only",sep = "_"))+viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="A")+theme(legend.position = "none" )+labs(title = idsign)))
      
       ### Also save the plot individually with the scale 
      to_save <- ((SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features =paste(idsign,"only",sep = "_"))+viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="A")+labs(fill=paste(idsign,"z-score",sep = "\n"))))
      ggsave(plot = to_save,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/",file,"_TLS_signatures_",idsign,"_zscore.pdf"),
         width = 3,height = 4)
      
    }else{
      SeuratSCT <- AddMetaData(SeuratSCT,as.vector(scale(apply(as.matrix(SeuratSCT[["SCT"]]@data[intersect_tls_sign,]),2,mean))),col.name = paste(idsign,"mean",sep = "_")) 
      #SeuratSCT <- AddMetaData(SeuratSCT,as.vector(scale(apply(as.matrix(SeuratSCT[["SCT"]]@data[intersect_tls_sign,]),2,sum))),col.name = paste(idsign,"sum",sep = "_")) 
      TLSplot[[idsign]] <- ((SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features =paste(idsign,"mean",sep = "_"))+viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="A")+theme(legend.position = "none" )+labs(title = idsign)))#+(SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features =paste(idsign,"sum",sep = "_"))+viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="A")))
      
      ### Also save the plot individually with the scale 
      to_save <-((SpatialFeaturePlot(SeuratSCT,features =paste(idsign,"mean",sep = "_"))+viridis::scale_fill_viridis(option="A")+labs(fill=paste(idsign,"z-score",sep = "\n"))))
      ggsave(plot = to_save,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/",file,"_TLS_signatures_",idsign,"_zscore.pdf"),
         width = 3,height = 4)
    }
  }
    
  patch<-wrap_plots(TLSplot,nrow = 2)
  ggsave(plot = patch,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/",file,"_TLS_signatures_patchwork_9sign_zscore.pdf"),
         width = 12,height = 6)

  # Save the seurat object with SCT + Filter SPOT + Starfysh ratio + BayesSpace cluster + TLS sign score in
  saveRDS(object = SeuratSCT,file = paste0("PATH/",file,"_seurat_sct_BayesSpace_Starfysh_TLSsign.rds"))
  
}


```


### TLS cluster identification with SpaTopic metatopic

The goal is to use [SpaTopic package](https://compbionju.github.io/SpaTopic/) to integrate spatial clustering from BayesSpace and cell-type deconvolution from Starfysh and identify topic accross different slides - named meta topic - and potentially identify a metatopic corresponding to TLS (and thus having a cluster of TLS accross all slides in order to analyze the relationships of clonotypes/clones with TLS)

```{r,eval=FALSE}
# Install SpaTopic.
## NB : sf and alphanull packages are required. If not installed, the github SpaTopic installation will failed
# install.packages("alphahull")
# devtools::install_github('compbioNJU/SpaTopic')
```

#### CellTopics generation for each slide - Supplementary S7B

CellTopics corresponds to spatial clusters (BayesSpace) annotated with CellType deconvolution (Starfysh) information. It is done for each slide independently. Then it will be further clustered in meta topic similar across all slides (next section).

Note : the full optimisation procedure is provided here. Again some QC plot are not provided/not included in the article and their corresponding path can be not informative (old repository) but they can be totally reproduced after adjusting out directory path.

In the optimisation procedure, 2 parameters from SpaTopic (CellTopic function) were tested, either binarization=T or binarization=F (see script). Note that the final condition kept for the analysis was without binarization (F), but all the script is still provided for lines consistency.

CellTopic_plot function used in this script for Supplementary **Figure S7B**.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(SpaTopic)

SampleId <- Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id

IDmatch <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id
names(IDmatch) <- SampleId

#color scale
### For CellTopic clusters (from the celltopic github...)
   my_colors <- c("#66b803", "#f94144", "#f8961e", "#3574b8", "#DE77AE", "#9970AB", "#D5E4A2", "#71D0F5", "#B1746F", "#ADE2D0", "#20DE8BFF", "#CCDE8BFF", "#f7f31c", "#FFA88BFF", "#FF6A8BFF")
### For the 25 cellTypes
   TumorPalette<- colorRampPalette(c("grey", "black"))( 4 )
  names(TumorPalette) <- c("PT_like" ,"ProInflammatory"  ,  "EMT_like"  , "PI3K")
  MyeloPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("pink", "#E7298A"))( 4 )
  names(MyeloPalette) <- c("Macrophage.M1","Macrophage.M2"  , "Monocytes"  , "MDSC")
  BcellPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("darkorange", "red"))( 3 )
  names(BcellPalette) <- c("B.cells.naive","B.cells.memory"  , "Plasmablasts")
  TcellPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("green", "darkgreen"))( 4 )
  names(TcellPalette) <- c("Tcm" ,"Tem" ,  "Tfh",  "Treg")
  TfunctionPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "darkblue"))( 4 )
  names(TfunctionPalette) <- c( "Activated.CD8" ,"Precursor.exhaustion","Dysfunc.CD8",  "Terminal.exhaustion")
  CAFPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("chocolate","brown"))( 2 )
  names(CAFPalette) <-c("CAFs.MSC.iCAF.like"  ,    "CAFs.myCAF.like" )
  DCPalette <- colorRampPalette(c("violet","purple"))( 2 )
  names(DCPalette) <-c("cDC" ,  "pDC" )
  NKPalete <- c("#7DF9FF") 
  names(NKPalete)<-"NK"
  EndoPalete <- c("#FBE870") 
  names(EndoPalete)<- "Endothelial"
  CellPalette <- c(TumorPalette,MyeloPalette,BcellPalette,TcellPalette,TfunctionPalette,CAFPalette,DCPalette,NKPalete,EndoPalete)
  names(CellPalette)<-paste("Starfysh",names(CellPalette),sep = "_")


for(file in FileID){
  #Load final Seurat object
  Seurat<- readRDS(paste0("PATH/",file,"_seurat_sct_BayesSpace_Starfysh_TLSsign.rds"))
  
  # retrieve spot_celltype dataframe from Starfysh
  spot_celltype<-Seurat@meta.data[,(grepl("Starfysh",colnames(Seurat@meta.data))) & (colnames(Seurat@meta.data)!="Starfysh_hub")]
  
  # retrieve spot_clusters from BayesSpace cluster : HERE WITHOUT BINARIZATION, AFTER NAMED : NO_BIN
  spot_clusters <- Seurat@meta.data["BayesSpace_cluster"]
  
  # CellTopic with Starfysh deconvolution score and BayesSpace spatial clusters
   result_list <- CellTopic(
    spot_celltype = spot_celltype,
    spot_clusters = spot_clusters,
    cluster = "BayesSpace_cluster",
    num_topics = 13,
    percent = 0.7
  )
   result_list[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic <- factor(result_list[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic,
                                                  levels = str_sort(unique(result_list[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic),numeric = T))
   
   ##Add metadata to Seurat object and vizualise
   Seurat_list <-list() # create a list to store 2 Seurat per file / one No_Bin, one Bin. NB : only the final No_bin classification is provided because it is the one used for analysis. But you can reproduce the other one if wanted with the following script ...
   Seurat_list[["No_bin"]] <- AddMetaData(Seurat, result_list[["CellTopic"]])
   p1<-(SpatialDimPlot(Seurat_list[["No_bin"]] , group.by = "CellTopic", image.alpha = 0, pt.size.factor =2)+ scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors)+ggtitle( "CellTopic"))
   ggsave(plot = p1,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/",file,"_SpaTopic_CellTopic.pdf"),
         width = 6,height = 5)
   
   ##same but binarized : AFTER NAMED BIN
   result_list_bin <- CellTopic(
    spot_celltype = spot_celltype,
    spot_clusters = spot_clusters,
    cluster = "BayesSpace_cluster",
    num_topics = 13,
    percent = 0.7,
    Binarization = T
  )
   ## 
   result_list_bin[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic <- factor(result_list_bin[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic,
                                                  levels = str_sort(unique(result_list_bin[["CellTopic"]]$CellTopic),numeric = T))
   
   Seurat_list[["Bin"]] <- AddMetaData(Seurat, result_list_bin[["CellTopic"]])
   p2<-(SpatialDimPlot(Seurat_list[["Bin"]], group.by = "CellTopic", image.alpha = 0, pt.size.factor =2)+ scale_fill_manual(values = my_colors)+ggtitle("CellTopic Binarization"))
      ggsave(plot = p2,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/",file,"_SpaTopic_CellTopicBin.pdf"),
         width = 6,height = 5)
      
   patch<-p1+p2
   ggsave(plot = patch,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/",file,"_SpaTopic_CellTopic_and_CellTopicBin.pdf"),
         width = 12,height = 5)

   
   #### NB : The following CellTopic_plot was used to generate the plot S7B (for slide SP_LHD6US, Cell Topic n°3)
   
   #celltopic plot for each Topic
   for(topic in levels(Seurat_list[["No_bin"]]$CellTopic)){
     plot<-CellTopic_plot(Seurat_list[["No_bin"]], 
               celltype_topic = result_list[["celltype_topic"]], 
               celltopic = topic,
               cols.highlight = c("#DE2D26", "#FEE0D2"),
               cols.celltype = CellPalette, 
               pt.size.factor = 2.2)
     ggsave(plot = plot,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/",file,"_SpaTopic_CellTopic_",topic,".pdf"),
         width = 5,height = 6)
   }
   ##Same for CellTopic_bin
   for(topic in levels(Seurat_list[["Bin"]]$CellTopic)){
     plot<-CellTopic_plot(Seurat_list[["Bin"]], 
               celltype_topic = result_list_bin$celltype_topic, 
               celltopic = topic,
               cols.highlight = c("#DE2D26", "#FEE0D2"),
               cols.celltype = CellPalette, 
               pt.size.factor = 2.2)
     ggsave(plot = plot,
         filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/",file,"_SpaTopic_CellTopicBIN_",topic,".pdf"),
         width = 5,height = 6)
   }
   
   ## Save Seurat
   saveRDS(object = Seurat_list,
           file = paste0("PATH/",file,"_seurat_sct_BayesSpace_Starfysh_TLSsign_SpaTopic_List_Bin_or_not.rds"))
   
   SpaTopic_list <-list()
   SpaTopic_list[["No_bin"]]<-result_list
   SpaTopic_list[["Bin"]]<-result_list_bin
   saveRDS(object = SpaTopic_list,
           file = paste0("PATH/",file,"_SpaTopic_List_Bin_or_not_allResults.rds"))
   
}
```

#### Meta Topic similar across all slides by clustering all CellTopics

Then from each CellTopic (from each slide), identify meta topics across slides.
Note : it was first done by hierarchical clustering, as in SpaTopic iniital article. But it necessitate to use an arbitrary threshold to cut the tree. So it was then done with MOVICS methods (see after).

##### S7C - hclust method

First cluster CellTopics by hierarchical clustering method (similar as SpaTopic workflow).
Initially used as a clustering method, finally used for illustration in supplmentary Figure **S7C**.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(SpaTopic)
library(reshape2)

SampleId <- Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id

IDmatch <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id
names(IDmatch) <- SampleId

# anonym_id
AnoCorresp <- setNames(Anonym_table$Anonym_id,nm = Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id) # correspondance with anonym 

   my_colors <- c("#66b803", "#f94144", "#f8961e", "#3574b8", "#DE77AE", "#9970AB", "#D5E4A2", "#71D0F5", "#B1746F", "#ADE2D0", "#20DE8BFF", "#CCDE8BFF", "#f7f31c", "#FFA88BFF", "#FF6A8BFF")

CellTypeTopic_list<-list()
for(file in SampleId){
  #Load SpaTopic results and retrieve the celltype topic proportion
  SpaTopicRes<-readRDS(paste0("PATH/",file,"_SpaTopic_List_Bin_or_not_allResults.rds"))
  
  #Convert matrix as data.frame
  SpaTopicRes <- lapply(SpaTopicRes,function(list){
    tmp<-data.frame(list[["celltype_topic"]])
    #### Anonymize and keep only 3 last character to make it more readable
    simply_ano <- substr(AnoCorresp[[file]],start = nchar(AnoCorresp[[file]])-2,stop = nchar(AnoCorresp[[file]]))
    colnames(tmp)<-paste(simply_ano,colnames(tmp),sep = "_")
    tmp$CellType <- rownames(tmp)
    tmp
  })
  CellTypeTopic_list[[file]] <-SpaTopicRes
}
 
CellTypeTopic_merged <- lapply(c(No_bin="No_bin",Bin="Bin"),function(bin){
  Sub<- lapply(CellTypeTopic_list,function(id)id[[bin]])
  Sub <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "CellType"), Sub)
  rownames(Sub)<-Sub$CellType
  corr <- round(cor(Sub[,setdiff(colnames(Sub),"CellType")]), 3)
})
 
for(bin in names(CellTypeTopic_merged)){
  corr<-CellTypeTopic_merged[[bin]]
  
  ##### SUPPLEMENTARY FIGURE S7C : WHEN bin == No_bin (no binarization)
  
  pdf(file = paste0(res_folder,"S7C_SpaTopic_Correlation_CellTopics_",bin,".pdf"))
    p <- pheatmap::pheatmap(corr,
             border_color = "black",
             scale = "none", 
             cluster_rows = T,
             cluster_cols = T,
             legend = TRUE,
             show_rownames = T,
             show_colnames = T,
             #cutree_rows = 11,
             #cutree_cols = 11,
             fontsize = 8,
             main = paste("Similarity of CellTopics in cell-type compositions -",bin))
    print(p)
  dev.off()
}

```

##### MetaTopics with MOVICS clusters - Main Figure 2B, 2C & Supplementary Figure S7D, S7E, S7F

Choose optimal nnumber of k clusters with MOVICS method.

Contains also the scripts for following plots :

Main Figure 2B, 2C & Supplementary Figure S7D, S7E, S7F

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(SpaTopic)
library(reshape2)
library(MOVICS)
library(ggalluvial)

SampleId <- Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id

IDmatch <- Anonym_table$SpatialGEX_id
names(IDmatch) <- SampleId

# anonym_id
AnoCorresp <- setNames(Anonym_table$Anonym_id,nm = Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id) # correspondance with anonym 

   my_colors <- c("#66b803", "#f94144", "#f8961e", "#3574b8", "#DE77AE", "#9970AB", "#D5E4A2", "#71D0F5", "#B1746F", "#ADE2D0", "#20DE8BFF", "#CCDE8BFF", "#f7f31c", "#FFA88BFF", "#FF6A8BFF")

CellTypeTopic_list<-list()
for(file in SampleId){
  #Load SpaTopic results and retrieve the celltype topic proportion
  SpaTopicRes<-readRDS(paste0("PATH/",file,"_SpaTopic_List_Bin_or_not_allResults.rds"))
  
  #Convert matrix as data.frame
  SpaTopicRes <- lapply(SpaTopicRes,function(list){
    tmp<-data.frame(list[["celltype_topic"]])
    #### Anonymize and keep only 3 last character to make it more readable
    simply_ano <- substr(AnoCorresp[[file]],start = nchar(AnoCorresp[[file]])-2,stop = nchar(AnoCorresp[[file]]))
    colnames(tmp)<-paste(simply_ano,colnames(tmp),sep = "_")
    tmp$CellType <- rownames(tmp)
    tmp
  })
  CellTypeTopic_list[[file]] <-SpaTopicRes
}
 
CellTypeTopic_merged <- lapply(c(No_bin="No_bin",Bin="Bin"),function(bin){
  Sub<- lapply(CellTypeTopic_list,function(id)id[[bin]])
  Sub <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "CellType"), Sub)
  rownames(Sub)<-Sub$CellType
  corr <- round(cor(Sub[,setdiff(colnames(Sub),"CellType")]), 3)
})

#################################################################
##  choose the optimal cluster number with MOVICS package
####################################################
for(bin in names(CellTypeTopic_merged)){
  #retrive the correlation matrix
  Sub<- lapply(CellTypeTopic_list,function(id)id[[bin]])
  Sub <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "CellType"), Sub)
  rownames(Sub)<-Sub$CellType
  Sub<-as.matrix(Sub[,setdiff(colnames(Sub),"CellType")])
  corr <- round(cor(Sub), 3)
  
  #get optimal number of k clusters with MOVICS getClusNum
  ##First on the matrix of cellTopic x cell type
  ### NB : duplicates the matrix because the MOVICS package is originaly for multi-omics
  optk <- getClustNum(data= list(matrix=Sub,
                                 dupli=Sub),#same matrix duplicated so that the package run
              is.binary = c(F,F),  
              try.N.clust = 2:16, # try cluster number from 2 to 16
              fig.path =paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/CellType_CellTopic_Matrix/"),
              fig.name = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_ClustNum_CellTypeMatrix.pdf"))
  
  ##Second on the CellTopics correlation matrix
  optk_corr <- getClustNum(data= list(matrix=corr,
                                 dupli=corr),#same matrix duplicated so that the package run
              is.binary = c(F,F),  
              try.N.clust = 2:16,  # try cluster number from 2 to 16
              fig.path =paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/Correlation_matrix/"),
              fig.name = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_ClustNum_CorrelationMatrix.pdf"))
  
  ##USe the MOVICS package to test multiple clustering algorithm at once and get a consensus
  ### Test number of clusters between 2 and 12. Store the results in a subFolder
  color<-c( "#023E8A", "#9D4EDD","#66b803",  "#f94144" ,  "#f8961e"  , "#3574b8"  ,"#DE77AE"  , "#9970AB",   "#D5E4A2"   ,"#71D0F5"  , "#B1746F" , "#ADE2D0"  , "#20DE8BFF","#f7f31c"  , "#FFA88BFF", "#FF6A8BFF",  "#011627")
  List_MOIC_Nclust<-list()
  
  Num_clust_bin<-list(No_bin=2:12,Bin=2:11)
  for(N_clust in Num_clust_bin[[bin]]){
    moic.res.list<- getMOIC(data = list(matrix=Sub,
                                 dupli=Sub),#same matrix duplicated so that the package run,
                         methodslist = list("SNF", "PINSPlus", "NEMO", "COCA", "LRAcluster", "ConsensusClustering", "IntNMF", "CIMLR", "MoCluster","iClusterBayes"),
                         N.clust = N_clust,
                         type = c("gaussian", "gaussian"))
    
     #consensus cluster heatmap
     cmoic<-getConsensusMOIC(moic.res.list = moic.res.list,
                            fig.path =paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/CellType_CellTopic_Matrix/"),
                               fig.name      = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_nclust_",N_clust,"_ConsensusHeatmap.pdf"),
                               distance      = "euclidean",
                            clust.col = color,
                               linkage       = "average")
    #save silouette plot
    getSilhouette(sil = cmoic$sil, # a sil object returned by getConsensusMOIC()
              fig.path = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/CellType_CellTopic_Matrix/"),
              fig.name = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_nclust_",N_clust,"_SilhouettePlot.pdf"),
             clust.col = color,
               height   = 7,
              width    = 10)
    #Save results
     List_MOIC_Nclust[[paste0("n",N_clust)]] <- list(moic_CellType=moic.res.list,
        cmoic_CellType=cmoic)
     
     ## Same but with correlation matrix 
     moic.res.list<-NULL
     moic.res.list<- getMOIC(data = list(matrix=corr,
                                 dupli=corr),#same matrix duplicated so that the package run,
                         methodslist = list("SNF", "PINSPlus", "NEMO", "COCA", "LRAcluster", "ConsensusClustering", "IntNMF", "CIMLR", "MoCluster","iClusterBayes"),
                         N.clust = N_clust,
                         type = c("gaussian", "gaussian"))
    
     #consensus cluster heatmap
     cmoic<-getConsensusMOIC(moic.res.list = moic.res.list,
                            fig.path =paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/Correlation_matrix/"),
                               fig.name      = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_nclust_",N_clust,"_ConsensusHeatmap.pdf"),
                               distance      = "euclidean",
                            clust.col = color,
                               linkage       = "average")
    #save silouette plot
    getSilhouette(sil = cmoic$sil, # a sil object returned by getConsensusMOIC()
              fig.path = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/Correlation_matrix/"),
              fig.name = paste0("SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_nclust_",N_clust,"_SilhouettePlot.pdf"),
             clust.col = color,
               height   = 7,
              width    = 10)
    #Save results
     List_MOIC_Nclust[[paste0("n",N_clust)]] <- c(List_MOIC_Nclust[[paste0("n",N_clust)]],list(moic_Corr=moic.res.list,
        cmoic_Corr=cmoic))
  }#end N_clust loop
  
  #Make an elbow plot of average silouette and k to choose best k which should have the highest average silouhette score.
  ## Generate a data.frame of k and average silouhette
  df_list <- lapply(setNames(Num_clust_bin[[bin]],paste0("n",Num_clust_bin[[bin]])),function(k){
    tmp_list <-List_MOIC_Nclust[[paste0("n",k)]]
    list(cmoic_CellType=data.frame(Num_clust=k,MeanSil=mean(as.data.frame(tmp_list$cmoic_CellType$sil)$sil_width)),
         cmoic_Corr=data.frame(Num_clust=k,MeanSil=mean(as.data.frame(tmp_list$cmoic_Corr$sil)$sil_width)))
  })
  df_list_cell<-Reduce(rbind,lapply(df_list,function(list)list$cmoic_CellType))
  plot<-ggplot(df_list_cell,aes(x=Num_clust,y=MeanSil))+
    geom_point()+
    geom_line(aes(group=0))+
    theme_bw()+
    labs(title = "Optimization of k clusters - Consensus of 10 clustering methods",
         subtitle = paste("CellTopic x CellType matrix -",bin),
         x="Number of k cluster",
         y="Average silouhette score")+
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = Num_clust_bin[[bin]])
  
  ### SUPPLEMENTARY PLOT S7D (if bin==No_bin)
  
    ggsave(plot = plot,
           filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/CellType_CellTopic_Matrix/","SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_consensusClust","_Silhouette_x_kCluster.pdf"),
           height =4 ,width = 6)
  
    ## Same but for correlation matrx
    df_list_corr<-Reduce(rbind,lapply(df_list,function(list)list$cmoic_Corr))
    plot<-ggplot(df_list_corr,aes(x=Num_clust,y=MeanSil))+
    geom_point()+
    geom_line(aes(group=0))+
    theme_bw()+
    labs(title = "Optimization of k clusters - Consensus of 10 clustering methods",
         subtitle = paste("CellTopic x CORRELATION matrix -",bin),
         x="Number of k cluster",
         y="Average silouhette score")+
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = Num_clust_bin[[bin]])
    ggsave(plot = plot,
           filename = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/Correlation_matrix/","SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MOVICS_consensusClust","_Silhouette_x_kCluster.pdf"),
           height =4 ,width = 6)
    
}# end bin loop

  Sub<-as.matrix(Sub[,setdiff(colnames(Sub),"CellType")])

  ##USe the MOVICS package to test multiple clustering algorithm at once and get a consensus
  ### Test number of clusters between 2 and 12. Store the results in a subFolder
  color<-c( "#023E8A", "#9D4EDD","#66b803",  "#f94144" ,  "#f8961e"  , "#3574b8"  ,"#DE77AE"  , "#9970AB",   "#D5E4A2"   ,"#71D0F5"  , "#B1746F" , "#ADE2D0"  , "#20DE8BFF","#f7f31c"  , "#FFA88BFF", "#FF6A8BFF",  "#011627")
  
  moic.res.list<- getMOIC(data = list(matrix=Sub,
                                 dupli=Sub),#same matrix duplicated so that the package run,

  #save silouette plot

  ##Retrieve cell_type

  Meta_CellTopic_cluster_long <- reshape::melt(cell_df, id.vars = c("MetaTopics", "Row.names", "sample"))

  df <- Meta_CellTopic_cluster_long %>% 
  group_by(MetaTopics, celltype_min) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm=T)) %>%
  spread(celltype_min, mean) %>%
  tibble::column_to_rownames(var = "MetaTopics")
  df<-df[str_order(rownames(df),numeric = T),]
  
  df_p <- unique(Meta_CellTopic_cluster_long$celltype_min) %>% as.data.frame() %>% tibble::column_to_rownames(var = ".")
  
  ct_n <- 1

      for(cls in unique(Meta_CellTopic_cluster_long$MetaTopics)){

  pdf(file = paste0(res_folder,"00_TLS_identification/SpaTopics/MOVICS_consensus/","SpaTopic_CellTopics_",bin,"_MetaTopicMOVICS_n",Num_clust_bin[[bin]],"_heatmap_AverageCellTypePerMetaTopic.pdf"),width = 10,height = 6)
```

### READ QC - Fastp FastQC

Run Fastp on fastq.gz file

```{bash,eval=F}
# in a conda environment : conda activate fastp

mkdir PATH/Processed_3rdRun

input_dir="PATH/RAWDATA_3rdRun_SMRTbellCRC/5960-BioniKK/CCS-Demultiplex/call-auto_ccs_outputs_barcoded/"

# write file input names for raw reads in a txt file
# Create a file of barcode for matching and use of grep on a file
# Grep file with barcode to get corresponding sample name

#Moove to out_dir : Immcantation_dir
LongRead_dir="PATH/Processed_3rdRun/"

input_file="${LongRead_dir}input_file_names_batch1_run3_SMRTbellCRC.txt"
output_file="${LongRead_dir}sampleId_batch1_run3_SMRTbellCRC.txt"

cd $LongRead_dir

mkdir Fastp

# check that file exists
if [ ! -f "$input_file" ] || [ ! -f "$output_file" ]; then
    echo "Les fichiers d'entrée ou de sortie n'existent pas."
    exit 1
fi

# open files
exec 3< "$input_file"
exec 4< "$output_file"

# reads line by line
while read -u 3 file_in && read -u 4 file_out; do
    # print file names to check
    echo "File in: $file_in"
    echo "File out: $file_out"

    # code
    echo "run fastqc"
    fastqc -o "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/" -t 16 "${input_dir}${file_in}"
    
    echo "run fastp"
    fastp --in1 "${input_dir}${file_in}" --out1 "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/${file_out}_fastp_processed.reads.fastq" --json "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/${file_out}_fastp.json" --html "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/${file_out}_fastp.html" --length_required=35 --dont_eval_duplication --thread=16 > "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/${file_out}_fastp.log" 2>&1

    # end
    echo "complete"

done

# close files
exec 3<&-
exec 4<&-

# conda deactivate


```

Reads from PacBio are CCS (Circular Consensus Sequencing) reads. There are generated from the polymerase reads containing at least 2 full-pass subreads from the insert (read in forward and read in reverse of the insert). There are highly accurate. There are no reads filtered by Fastp software with default value (and only 1-2% of read below Q20).

### Preprocess Long read

Then Pipeline from [Immcantation Immcantation for Illumina 5'RACE BCR mRNA](https://Immcantation.readthedocs.io/en/stable/workflows/VanderHeiden2017_Workflow.html) / and from [Engblom et al long read processing](https://github.com/HoseinT/long-read-processing-STAR-paper/blob/main/run86.py) are adapted for identifying :

Long reads from PacBio converted in ccs are processed as follow :

- Reads with overall quality bellow 20 are filtered with Immcantation FilterSeq.py  
- Reads are reverse complemented with seqtk  
- Illumina partialRead1 and TSO primers are aligned against original reads and reverse complemented reads with MaskPrimers.py align with the parameter --tag  
- Log from MaskPrimers.py are converted in tabulated file in order to search for a TTTT sequence after the partialR1 primer in forward and reverse orientations. If no TTTT sequence is found after the primer (after 17 bases of the primer and 28 bases of the SB and UMI) or if TTTT sequence is found is both orientations (forward and reverse), reads are filtered. Then, only reads with a unique combination of partialR1, TTTT, and TSO orientations are kept (i.e. if partialR1 are fully aligned in both direction, then the read is filtered - if no TSO is found, the read is filtered, etc). Finally, if the TSO is found before the partialR1 in the unique orientation valid, then reads are filtered. This allow to identify read header associated to correct forward and reverse reads (do not export header of read to filter)  
- Then back to fastq file (to retrieve quality data ...) use grep with the generated list of correct read header to generate 2 sub fastq files with correct forward and correct reverse reads respectively.  
- Use seqtk to reverse complement only reverse reads.  
- Concatenate back forward and reverse (reverse complemented) fastq in one unique fastq.  
- Use again MaskPrimers.py align with --cut parameter to identify partialR1 (hit are known) and with --tag parameter to identify TSO primer start.  
- Open the fastq file in R with ShortRead package. Identify SB as the 16 first bases (partialR1 has been cut) and the UMI as the 12 bases following, tag the header and cut them.  
- Check SB consistency against whitelist - correct if necessary. Filter polyT barcode if over-represented.    
- All reads must start with at least 4 T (TTTT). Identify the end of the polyT by the first base matching the pattern “[^T]T{0,2}[^T]T{0,2}[^T]” and cut the polydT.  
- Open the log file from MaskPrimer.py align on TSO to get the correct position of TSO start. Trim after TSO and trim 9 bases before (9 first bases of TSO were not aligned with MaskPrimer.py. As in SpatialVDJ paper).  
- Write the final fastq file.  

#### Identify partR1 and TSO in reads

```{bash,eval=F}
# in a environment : conda activate pRESTO

LongRead_dir="PATH/Processed_3rdRun/"

cd ${LongRead_dir}

#List file 
files=`cat "${LongRead_dir}sampleId_batch1_run3_SMRTbellCRC.txt"`

mkdir Immcantation

mkdir Immcantation/pipeline_log
mkdir Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual
mkdir Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation

for file in $files; do

  echo $file

## FilterSeq Q20

echo "Runing FilterSeq.py quality on R1 to filter seq with average quality < 20"
FilterSeq.py quality -s "${LongRead_dir}Fastp/${file}_fastp_processed.reads.fastq" -q 20 --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/" --outname "${file}_R1" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_FS.log" > "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

done

# conda deactivate

## conda activate seqtk
## seqtk seq -r to create a reverse complement the file and perform the alignment back in

LongRead_dir="PATH/Processed_3rdRun/"

cd ${LongRead_dir}

#List file 
files=`cat "${LongRead_dir}sampleId_batch1_run3_SMRTbellCRC.txt"`

for file in $files; do

  echo $file
  
  input_file="${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass.fastq"
  output_file="${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass_ReverseComp.fastq"
  
  seqtk seq -r $input_file > $output_file
  
done

## conda deactivate

## Create a fasta file with nano command containing the partR1 sequence to align : CGACGCTCTTCCGATCT
## Create a file for TSO primers in fasta just as for partR1. Seq : TCTGCGTTGATACCACT

## conda activate pRESTO

for file in $files; do

  echo $file

## MaskPrimers Align on partR1 only - On all the length of the long read - in forward direction only first and tag the position

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify partial R1 in forward read only"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/partR1.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode tag --pf PART_R1_FORWARD --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/" --outname "${file}" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_PartR1_Forward.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing ParseLog.py on R1 MaskPrimer log to identify PartR1 Start Forward"
ParseLog.py -l "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_PartR1_Forward.log" -f ID PRSTART ERROR INSEQ >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify TSO in forward read only"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/TSO.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode tag --pf TSO_FORWARD --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/" --outname "${file}" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_TSO_Forward.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing ParseLog.py on R1 MaskPrimer log to identify TSO Start Forward"
ParseLog.py -l "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_TSO_Forward.log" -f ID PRSTART ERROR >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1



# Same on RevComp

## MaskPrimers Align on partR1 only - On all the length of the long read - in RevComp direction only first and tag the position

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify partial R1 in RevComp read only"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass_ReverseComp.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/partR1.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode tag --pf PART_R1_REVCOMP --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/" --outname "${file}" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_PartR1_RevComp.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing ParseLog.py on R1 MaskPrimer log to identify PartR1 Start RevComp"
ParseLog.py -l "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_PartR1_RevComp.log" -f ID PRSTART ERROR INSEQ >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify TSO in RevComp read only"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass_ReverseComp.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/TSO.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode tag --pf TSO_REVCOMP --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/" --outname "${file}" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_TSO_RevComp.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing ParseLog.py on R1 MaskPrimer log to identify TSO Start RevComp"
ParseLog.py -l "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_MP_Align_TSO_RevComp.log" -f ID PRSTART ERROR >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

done


```


#### Identify correct read orientation

Find read orientation

```{r,eval=F}
library(ggplot2)
## Check output from MaskPrimers.py align

# Open a file connection for writing a log file ##un comment if needed
sink(paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/","pipeline_log/","R_LongReads_Search_Orientation.log"), append = FALSE, type = c("output"))

  print("Start processing of Long read")
  Sys.time()
  
  #add space in the log
  print("\n")
  print("\n")
  
listfile<-list.files("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation",pattern ="table.tab" ,full.names = T)

SampleId <- unique(gsub("_MP_Align.*","",sapply(strsplit(listfile,"/"),function(x)x[length(x)])))
names(SampleId) <- SampleId

listLog<-list()
listLog <- lapply(SampleId,function(id){
  
  listfileId <- listfile[grepl(id,listfile)]
  
  tmp <- lapply(listfileId,function(file){
    tmpdf<-read.delim(file)
    File <- ifelse(grepl("PartR1_Forward",file),yes = "PartR1_Forward",
                   no = ifelse(grepl("PartR1_RevComp",file),yes = "PartR1_RevComp",
                   no = ifelse(grepl("TSO_Forward",file),yes = "TSO_Forward",
                   no = ifelse(grepl("TSO_RevComp",file),yes = "TSO_RevComp",no = "WTF"))))
    colnames(tmpdf) <- paste(File,colnames(tmpdf),sep = "_")
    colnames(tmpdf)[grepl("ID",colnames(tmpdf))] <- "ID"
    tmpdf
  })
  
  Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "ID", all = TRUE),tmp)
  
})

# Search for a polydT stretch after partR1 in INSEQ forward and RevComp
## PartR1 primer is 17 base long. After partR1 there should be 28 bp before polydT (16 for SB and 12 for UMI). Then search for 4T

## Note : PRSTART is 0 based - R is 1 based > Add 1 to take in consideration

for(Id in SampleId){
  tmp <- listLog[[Id]]
  tmp$PolyT_Forward_INSEQ <- ifelse(substr(x = tmp$PartR1_Forward_INSEQ,
                                           start = tmp$PartR1_Forward_PRSTART+1+17+28,
                                           stop = tmp$PartR1_Forward_PRSTART+1+20+28) == "TTTT",yes = "PolyT_Forward_correct",no = "PolyT_Forward_incorrect")
  
  tmp$PolyT_RevComp_INSEQ <- ifelse(substr(x = tmp$PartR1_RevComp_INSEQ,
                                           start = tmp$PartR1_RevComp_PRSTART+1+17+28,
                                           stop = tmp$PartR1_RevComp_PRSTART+1+20+28) == "TTTT",yes = "PolyT_RevComp_correct",no = "PolyT_RevComp_incorrect")
  
  listLog[[Id]] <- tmp
}


# Compute proportion of reads with correct polydT after partR1 in forward and reverse orientations

FindOrientation<-lapply(SampleId,function(Id){
  Num <- table(listLog[[Id]]$PolyT_Forward_INSEQ,listLog[[Id]]$PolyT_RevComp_INSEQ)
  Prop <- round((Num/sum(rowSums(Num)))*100,digits = 2)
  
  return(list(Num=Num,Prop=Prop))
}) 


#Print results of primer alignment and search for polydT
print("Identification of reads orientation and search for polydT")

for(Id in SampleId){
  print(as.character(Id))
  
  Num <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Num["PolyT_Forward_incorrect","PolyT_RevComp_incorrect"]
  Prop <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Prop["PolyT_Forward_incorrect","PolyT_RevComp_incorrect"]
  print(paste0("Reads without any correct polydT after partR1 : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  Num <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Num["PolyT_Forward_correct","PolyT_RevComp_incorrect"]
  Prop <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Prop["PolyT_Forward_correct","PolyT_RevComp_incorrect"]
  print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT only in Forward orientation : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  Num <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Num["PolyT_Forward_incorrect","PolyT_RevComp_correct"]
  Prop <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Prop["PolyT_Forward_incorrect","PolyT_RevComp_correct"]
  print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT only in Reverse orientation : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  Num <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Num["PolyT_Forward_correct","PolyT_RevComp_correct"]
  Prop <-FindOrientation[[Id]]$Prop["PolyT_Forward_correct","PolyT_RevComp_correct"]
  print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT in double orientation : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
}

#add space in the log
  print("\n")
  print("\n")


# Orient reads according to multiple parameters :

## Filter only reads with a correct polydT in one unique direction
  
print("Filter reads with correct polydT in unique orientation")

for(Id in SampleId){
  
  print(as.character(Id))
  
  tmp <- listLog[[Id]]
  
  tmp <-tmp[(tmp$PolyT_Forward_INSEQ=="PolyT_Forward_correct" & tmp$PolyT_RevComp_INSEQ=="PolyT_RevComp_incorrect") | (tmp$PolyT_Forward_INSEQ=="PolyT_Forward_incorrect" & tmp$PolyT_RevComp_INSEQ=="PolyT_RevComp_correct"),]

  listLog[[Id]] <- tmp
  
  print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT in unique orientation kept : ",nrow(tmp)))
  
  plot <- ggplot(listLog[[Id]],aes(x=PartR1_Forward_PRSTART,y=PartR1_Forward_ERROR,color=PolyT_Forward_INSEQ))+
  geom_point()+
    ggtitle("Forward orientation - Correct polydT after partR1")
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_LongRead_Process/",Id,"_Forward_orientation_Correct_polydT_after_partR1.pdf"),plot = plot,width = 7,height = 7)
  
  plot <- ggplot(listLog[[Id]],aes(x=PartR1_RevComp_PRSTART,y=PartR1_RevComp_ERROR,color=PolyT_RevComp_INSEQ))+
  geom_point()+
    ggtitle("Reverse orientation - Correct polydT after partR1")
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_LongRead_Process/",Id,"_Reverse_orientation_Correct_polydT_after_partR1.pdf"),plot = plot,width = 7,height = 7)
}
 
#add space in the log
  print("\n")
  print("\n")
 
# Identify correct orientation

print("Reads with correct orientation")

for(Id in SampleId){
  
  print(as.character(Id))
  
  tmp <- listLog[[Id]]
  
  tmp$PolyTOrientation <- NA
  
  tmp$PolyTOrientation <- ifelse(tmp$PolyT_Forward_INSEQ %in% "PolyT_Forward_correct",yes = "FwdPolyT",
         no = "RevPolyT")
  
  tmp$ReadStructure <- NA
  
  #Threshold of error could be 0.06 (1 error out of 17 for partR1 or TSO)
    partR1_forward_thresh <- ifelse(tmp$PartR1_Forward_ERROR==0,yes = "FwdPartR1full",no = ifelse(tmp$PartR1_Forward_ERROR <0.06,yes = "FwdPartR1<0.06",no = "FwdPartR1>=0.06"))
    
    partR1_reverse_thresh <- ifelse(tmp$PartR1_RevComp_ERROR==0,yes = "RevPartR1full",no = ifelse(tmp$PartR1_RevComp_ERROR <0.06,yes = "RevPartR1<0.06",no = "RevPartR1>=0.06"))
    
    TSO_forward_thresh <- ifelse(tmp$TSO_Forward_ERROR==0,yes = "FwdTSOfull",no = ifelse(tmp$TSO_Forward_ERROR <0.06,yes = "FwdTSO<0.06",no = "FwdTSO>=0.06"))
    
    TSO_reverse_thresh <- ifelse(tmp$TSO_RevComp_ERROR==0,yes = "RevTSOfull",no = ifelse(tmp$TSO_RevComp_ERROR <0.06,yes = "RevTSO<0.06",no = "RevTSO>=0.06"))
    
    tmp$ReadStructure <- paste(partR1_forward_thresh,partR1_reverse_thresh,tmp$PolyTOrientation,TSO_forward_thresh,TSO_reverse_thresh,sep = "_")
    
    
    TableStructure <- sort(table(tmp$ReadStructure),decreasing = T)
    TableStructureProp<-round((TableStructure/sum(TableStructure))*100,2)
    
    Num<-TableStructure[["FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06"]]
    Prop<-TableStructureProp[["FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06"]]
    print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT and full partR1 and TSO alignment only in Forward orientation : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    Num<-TableStructure[["FwdPartR1>=0.06_RevPartR1full_RevPolyT_FwdTSO>=0.06_RevTSOfull"]]
    Prop<-TableStructureProp[["FwdPartR1>=0.06_RevPartR1full_RevPolyT_FwdTSO>=0.06_RevTSOfull"]]
    print(paste0("Reads with correct polydT and full partR1 and TSO alignment only in Reverse orientation : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    Num<-sum(TableStructure[!(names(TableStructure) %in% c("FwdPartR1>=0.06_RevPartR1full_RevPolyT_FwdTSO>=0.06_RevTSOfull",
                            "FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06"))])
    Prop<-sum(TableStructureProp[!(names(TableStructureProp) %in% c("FwdPartR1>=0.06_RevPartR1full_RevPolyT_FwdTSO>=0.06_RevTSOfull",
                            "FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06"))])
    print(paste0("Reads with ambiguous partR1 or TSO alignment or incomplete structure : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    #filter only reads with full partR1 to TSO in forward or reverse
    tmp <- tmp[tmp$ReadStructure=="FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06" | tmp$ReadStructure=="FwdPartR1>=0.06_RevPartR1full_RevPolyT_FwdTSO>=0.06_RevTSOfull",]
    
    tmp$ReadOrientation <- NA
    tmp$ReadOrientation<- ifelse(tmp$ReadStructure=="FwdPartR1full_RevPartR1>=0.06_FwdPolyT_FwdTSOfull_RevTSO>=0.06",yes = "Forward",no = "Reverse")
    
    
    #Filter also reads with partR1 position in the same orientation as the TSO but TSO before partR1 ... 
    
    TmpForward <- tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Forward",]
    ForwardToFilter <- TmpForward$PartR1_Forward_PRSTART < TmpForward$TSO_Forward_PRSTART
    
    TableFilter <- table(ForwardToFilter)
    TableFilterProp <- round((TableFilter/sum(TableFilter))*100,2)
    
    Num<-TableFilter[["TRUE"]]
    Prop<-TableFilterProp[["TRUE"]]
    print(paste0("Reads in Forward orientation with all elements in correct order (partR1<polydT<TSO) : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    Num<-TableFilter[["FALSE"]]
    Prop<-TableFilterProp[["FALSE"]]
    print(paste0("Reads in Forward orientation with TSO before partR1 : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    TmpReverse <- tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Reverse",]
    ReverseToFilter <- TmpReverse$PartR1_RevComp_PRSTART < TmpReverse$TSO_RevComp_PRSTART
    
    TableFilter <- table(ReverseToFilter)
    TableFilterProp <- round((TableFilter/sum(TableFilter))*100,2)
    
    Num<-TableFilter[["TRUE"]]
    Prop<-TableFilterProp[["TRUE"]]
    print(paste0("Reads in Reverse orientation with all elements in correct order (partR1<polydT<TSO) : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    Num<-TableFilter[["FALSE"]]
    Prop<-TableFilterProp[["FALSE"]]
    print(paste0("Reads in Reverse orientation with TSO before partR1 : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
    
    #filter
    tmp <- rbind(TmpForward[ForwardToFilter,],TmpReverse[ReverseToFilter,])
    
   listLog[[Id]] <- tmp
} 
  

#add space in the log
  print("\n")
  print("\n")


# Plot PartialR1 position in read according to error and/or TSO position

for(Id in SampleId){
  
  tmp <-listLog[[Id]]
  
  plot <- ggplot(tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Forward",],aes(x=PartR1_Forward_PRSTART,y=TSO_Forward_PRSTART))+
  geom_point()+
    ggtitle("Forward orientation - Correct Read structure: partR1>polydT>TSO")
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_LongRead_Process/",Id,"_Forward_orientation_Correct_readStructure_partR1_polydT_TSO.pdf"),plot = plot,width = 7,height = 7)
  
  
  plot <- ggplot(tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Reverse",],aes(x=PartR1_RevComp_PRSTART,y=TSO_RevComp_PRSTART))+
  geom_point()+
    ggtitle("Reverse orientation - Correct Read structure: partR1>polydT>TSO")
  
  ggsave(filename = paste0(res_folder,"02_LongRead_Process/",Id,"_Reverse_orientation_Correct_readStructure_partR1_polydT_TSO.pdf"),plot = plot,width = 7,height = 7)
  

}

# Retrieve the list of reads ID in forward orientation and in reverse to select
for(Id in SampleId){
  tmp <-listLog[[Id]]
  
  ForwardReadId <- tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Forward","ID"]
  
  writeLines(ForwardReadId,paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/",Id,"_forward_readsId.txt"))
  
  ReverseReadId <- tmp[tmp$ReadOrientation=="Reverse","ID"]
  
  writeLines(ReverseReadId,paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/",Id,"_reverse_readsId.txt"))
}
  

sink()
```

#### Filter and orient correct reads

Filter reads without correct structure (partR1, TTTT, TSO) in fastq, reverse complement the reads in reverse orientation, cut partialR1 and identify TSO start (tag)

```{bash,eval=F}
## grep correct forward and correct reverse reads respectively in 2 different fastq files

LongRead_dir="PATH/Processed_3rdRun/"

cd ${LongRead_dir}

mkdir Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient

#List file 
files=`cat "${LongRead_dir}sampleId_batch1_run3_SMRTbellCRC.txt"`


for file in $files; do

  echo $file

## Grep correct forward reads

echo "Runing grep on seq in forward orientation to take only seq in forward"
grep -A 3 -f "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_forward_readsId.txt" "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass.fastq" | grep -v "^\-\-$" > "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_forward_reads.fastq"

## Grep correct reverse reads

echo "Runing grep on seq in reverse orientation to take only seq in reverse"
grep -A 3 -f "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/${file}_reverse_readsId.txt" "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/1_FilterSeqQual/${file}_R1_quality-pass_ReverseComp.fastq" | grep -v "^\-\-$" > "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_reverse_reads.fastq"

## Concatenate

echo "Runing cat to create a final fastq file containing all reads in correct orientation (reverse reads reverse complemented"
cat "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_forward_reads.fastq" "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_reverse_reads.fastq" > "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_all_reads.fastq"

done


# in a environment : conda activate pRESTO


for file in $files; do

  echo $file

## MaskPrimers.py align with --cut on partialR1

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify and cut partial R1 in all reads"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_correct_all_reads.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/partR1.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode cut --pf PART_R1 --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/" --outname "${file}_partR1" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_MP_Align_PartR1.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

## MAskPrimers.py align with --tag on TSO

echo "Runing MaskPrimers.py align to identify TSO position in all reads"
MaskPrimers.py align -s "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_partR1_primers-pass.fastq" -p "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/2_ReadOrientation/TSO.fasta" --maxlen 6000 --skiprc --maxerror 0.06 --mode tag --pf TSO --outdir "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/" --outname "${file}_partR1_TSO" --log "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_MP_Align_TSO.log" --nproc 20 >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

echo "Runing ParseLog.py on R1 MaskPrimer log to identify TSO Start Forward"
ParseLog.py -l "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/${file}_MP_Align_TSO.log" -f ID PRSTART ERROR >> "${LongRead_dir}Immcantation/pipeline_log/${file}_Immcantation_perf.log" 2>&1

done
```

#### Identify SB and UMI, trim polyT, trim TSO

```{r,eval=F}
#dir.create("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/4_TrimPrimerAndBarcode")

library(ShortRead)

# Open a file connection for writing a log file ##un comment if needed
sink(paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/","pipeline_log/","R_LongReads_Identify_barcodes.log"), append = FALSE, type = c("output"))

  print("Start processing of Long read")
  Sys.time()
  
  #add space in the log
  print("\n")
  print("\n")

SampleId <- Anonym_table$SpatialVDJ_id

for(id in SampleId){

  print(as.character(id))
  print(paste0("Start :",Sys.time()))
  
  # Load fastq file with ShortRead package
  fastq_file<-paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/",id,"_partR1_TSO_primers-pass.fastq")
  fastq<-ShortRead::readFastq(fastq_file)
  
  # Identify spatial barcode (SB) 
  
  ## Take 16 first base as SB and trim from reads (and quality sequence)
  SB <- substr(fastq@sread,1,16)
  fastq@sread <- DNAStringSet(substr(fastq@sread,17,nchar(fastq@sread)))
  fastq@quality@quality <- BStringSet(substr(fastq@quality@quality,17,nchar(fastq@quality@quality)))
  
  ## Filter or correct SB with whitelist 
  WhiteList <- read.delim("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/4_TrimPrimerAndBarcode/visium-v1.txt",header = F)
  
  SBinWhiteList <- SB %in% WhiteList$V1 # evaluate if SB exist in Whitelist
  
  SBcorrected <- NULL
  TableBarcode <- NULL
  for(i in 1:length(SB)){
    if(SBinWhiteList[[i]]){
      SBcorrected <- c(SBcorrected,SB[[i]])
      TableBarcode <- c(TableBarcode,"Original_SB")
    }else{
      # if only 1 barcode in whitelist differ from 1 hamming distance, then barcode is corrected. Otherwise the sequence should be filtered
      Dist<-(stringdist::stringdist(a = SB[[i]],b = WhiteList$V1,method="hamming"))
      TableDist <- table(Dist)
      if("1" %in% names(TableDist)){
        SBcorrected<-c(SBcorrected,ifelse(test = TableDist[["1"]]==1,
             yes = WhiteList$V1[which(Dist==1)],
             no = "To_filter")) 
        TableBarcode <- c(TableBarcode,ifelse(test = TableDist[["1"]]==1,
             yes = "Corrected_SB",
             no = "Filtered_Seq")) 
      }else{
        SBcorrected<- c(SBcorrected,"To_filter") 
        TableBarcode <- c(TableBarcode,"Filtered_Seq")
      }

    }
  }
  
  TableBarcode <- table(TableBarcode)
  TableBarcodeProp <- round((TableBarcode/sum(TableBarcode))*100,2)
  
  Num <-ifelse(test = "Original_SB" %in% names(TableBarcode),
               yes =TableBarcode[["Original_SB"]] ,
               no = 0)
  Prop <-ifelse(test = "Original_SB" %in% names(TableBarcodeProp),
               yes =TableBarcodeProp[["Original_SB"]] ,
               no = 0)
  print(paste0("Reads with a SB present in whitelist : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  Num <-ifelse(test = "Corrected_SB" %in% names(TableBarcode),
               yes =TableBarcode[["Corrected_SB"]] ,
               no = 0)
  Prop <-ifelse(test = "Corrected_SB" %in% names(TableBarcodeProp),
               yes =TableBarcodeProp[["Corrected_SB"]] ,
               no = 0)
  print(paste0("Reads with a SB corrected with whitelist : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  Num <-ifelse(test = "Filtered_Seq" %in% names(TableBarcode),
               yes =TableBarcode[["Filtered_Seq"]] ,
               no = 0)
  Prop <-ifelse(test = "Filtered_Seq" %in% names(TableBarcodeProp),
               yes =TableBarcodeProp[["Filtered_Seq"]] ,
               no = 0)
  print(paste0("Reads with incorrect SB according to whitelist : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  ##Tag header with SBcorrected
  if(length(unique(SBcorrected))>4992)stop("Spatial barcode diversity too high")
  
  fastq@id <- BStringSet(paste0(fastq@id,"|SB=",SBcorrected))
  
  ## Filter seq with SBcorrected == "To_filter"
  fastq<-fastq[SBcorrected!="To_filter"]
  
  
  # Identify UMI (and filter TTTTTTTTTTTTTTTT UMI if the top one)
  
  ## Take 12 first base as UMI and trim from reads (and quality sequence)
  UMI <- substr(fastq@sread,1,12)
  fastq@sread <- DNAStringSet(substr(fastq@sread,13,nchar(fastq@sread)))
  fastq@quality@quality <- BStringSet(substr(fastq@quality@quality,13,nchar(fastq@quality@quality)))
  fastq@id <- BStringSet(paste0(fastq@id,"|UMI=",UMI))

  # TRIM TSO (INSERT_END)
  TSOstart <- read.delim(paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/3_FilterAndOrient/",id,"_MP_Align_TSO_table.tab"))
  rownames(TSOstart) <- gsub("ccs.*","ccs",TSOstart$ID) ## rename read ID without the tag - Keep only header
  TSOstart <- TSOstart[gsub("ccs.*","ccs",fastq@id),] # filter and order df in the same order as fastq object
  
  fastq@sread <- DNAStringSet(substr(fastq@sread,1,TSOstart$PRSTART+1-28-9-1)) # TRIM until TSO start. +1 because PRSTART is in base 0 but R is in base 1. -28 for SB and UMI that were extracted above. -9 because 9 first base from TSO were not aligned with MaskPrimers.py align. -1 because I want to get all the base before TSO ...
  fastq@quality@quality <- BStringSet(substr(fastq@quality@quality,1,TSOstart$PRSTART+1-28-9-1))
  
  
   # Identify first base after polydT (INSERT_START)  by the first match with the pattern : “[^T]T{0,2}[^T]T{0,2}[^T]”
  
  INSERT_Start<-stringr::str_locate(as.character(fastq@sread), '[^T]T{0,2}[^T]T{0,2}[^T]')[,"start"]
  
  # Filter Read with only a polyT (it happended for 2 reads for SP_0O0B5S)
  Insert <-substr(fastq@sread,INSERT_Start,nchar(fastq@sread))
  
  Num <- sum(is.na(Insert))
  Prop <- round((Num/length(fastq))*100,2)
  print(paste0("Reads with only polyT in insert filtered : ",Num," (",Prop,"%)"))
  
  fastq <- fastq[!is.na(Insert)] ## filter and keep non only polyT seq
  INSERT_Start<- INSERT_Start[!is.na(Insert)] ## filter and keep non only polyT seq
  
  fastq@id <- BStringSet(paste0(fastq@id,"|PolyT=",substr(fastq@sread,1,INSERT_Start-1)))
  fastq@sread <- DNAStringSet(substr(fastq@sread,INSERT_Start,nchar(fastq@sread)))
  fastq@quality@quality <- BStringSet(substr(fastq@quality@quality,INSERT_Start,nchar(fastq@quality@quality)))
  
  # Write reads to new fastq file
  ShortRead::writeFastq(fastq,paste0("PATH/Processed_3rdRun/Immcantation/4_TrimPrimerAndBarcode/",id,"_only_insert.fastq"),compress=F)
  
  
  print(paste0("End :",Sys.time()))
}


sink()
```
